newsitem.title: USA: NYC to pick bond firms for new agency in June.
newsitem.headline: NYC to pick bond firms for new agency in June.

text.p: New York City will likely complete the selection of municipal underwriters for its new financing authority in June, city budget director Joseph Lhota said Thursday.
"The time frame for the announcement probably will be sometime in June," Lhota said.

Lhota explained the city started interviewing bond firms this week and that the evaluations probably would stretch into next month. Previously, city officials have said the selections might be made as soon as May.
Albany early this year approved the New York City Transitional Finance Authority, giving the city the ability to issue about $7.5 billion of debt.
The Authority plans to start selling debt in late August or early September, with roughly $1.3 billion of sales anticipated for fiscal 1998.

Bond underwriters are keenly awaiting the city's decision on which firms will get to underwrite the new Authority's debt, as city officials have said the selections might cause them to reshuffle the present syndicates New York City uses to sell its general obligation and water bonds.
